text: As freedom came closer, the deep split between the Congress and the Muslim League led by
Muhammad Ali Jinnah could not be bridged.
The League demanded a separate country for Muslims, Pakistan.
In the end, Britain agreed to divide the land.
The border was drawn by a British lawyer, Cyril Radcliffe, who had never been to India.
He was given about five weeks, five weeks, to divide 400 million people.
At midnight on the 15th of August, 1947, India became free.
In Delhi, Jawaharlal Nehru, the first prime minister, told the assembly that India had made a tryst with destiny.
At the stroke of midnight, while the world slept, India would awake to life and freedom.
But the border was only announced two days later, and across Punjab and Bengal, millions
of people suddenly found themselves on the wrong side.
What followed was one of the largest migrations in human history.
